facts.claim: Castlemaine is a gold-rush boomtown founded in 1851 in Victoria's Goldfields, about 123 km by road from Melbourne and 39 km from Bendigo, with a population of 7,506 in 2021.
The Theatre Royal, established in 1854, is the oldest continuously operating theatre in mainland Australia.
Grand gold-era architecture and Victorian hotels survive on most street corners, alongside mullock heaps and mine shafts in Castlemaine Diggings National Heritage Park.
The town has a vibrant arts scene and is popular with travellers from Melbourne; trains on the Bendigo line run roughly hourly and take about 90 minutes.

Maldon, 19 km away, was declared 'Australia's first notable town' by the National Trust of Victoria in 1966 for its largely unchanged 1850s gold-town buildings, and one mine there is still open to the public.
A steam railway runs from Castlemaine station to Maldon on most Fridays, Saturdays and Sundays.

experiences: See a show at Australia's oldest running theatre

tips.title: Steam train to Maldon
tips.detail: The Victorian Goldfields Railway runs from Castlemaine station to Maldon mostly on Fridays to Sundays, so plan weekend visits around it.

tips.title: Stay on marked tracks
tips.detail: Open mine shafts and mullock heaps sit off the marked goldfields trails, so keep to signed paths when bushwalking.

best_months.rationale: Autumn and spring suit walking the diggings and the Maldon streets (inland Victoria; no sourced statement, judgement from inland-Victoria climate: UNVERIFIED, needs a visitor-source check).

facts.claim: Apollo Bay is a coastal town on the Great Ocean Road on the eastern side of Cape Otway, with a population of 1,790 in 2021, about 191 km from Melbourne.
Cape Otway Lightstation, about 30 minutes' drive away, has operated since 1848 and is the oldest surviving lighthouse on mainland Australia.
Southern right whales come to the area from winter to spring to breed and calve, and the Cape Otway lighthouse is a vantage point for land-based whale watching.
The Great Ocean Walk is a 104 km route through beaches, rainforest and seaside towns that passes through Apollo Bay on its way to the Twelve Apostles.
Maits Rest is a 30-minute rainforest boardwalk with glow worms at night; the Otway Fly is a steel canopy walk 600 m long and up to 47 m high.
The Otway Fly claims to be the longest and highest steel canopy walk in the world and also offers zip-line tours.

experiences: Watch whales from the coast in winter and spring
Hike sections of the Great Ocean Walk

tips.title: Faster route via Colac
tips.detail: Driving via Colac is much quicker than the Great Ocean Road, so use the coast road when you have time for the scenery.

tips.title: Book Great Ocean Walk camps
tips.detail: The walk's designated campsites have limited numbers and must be booked beforehand.

tips.title: Marriner's Falls track closed
tips.detail: Parks Victoria closed the walking track to Marriner's Falls in 2011 over falling-tree risk, so check access before driving out.

best_months.rationale: Warm months suit the coast, beaches and Great Ocean Walk (judgement, UNVERIFIED by a source); whales visit winter to spring, covered by the seasonal tag.

seasonal_tags: whale watching, winter to spring (southern right whales breed and calve; exact months unverified)

facts.claim: Wangaratta is a city of 29,808 people (2021) in north-east Victoria, 236 km from Melbourne on the Hume Freeway, at the junction of the Ovens and King rivers.
Wangaratta is the start of the Murray to the Mountains Rail Trail, a sealed off-road route of about 95 km.
Glenrowan, 14 km away, is where bushranger Ned Kelly made his last stand in 1880, and it gives its name to a wine region where vines were first planted in 1866.
A dozen wineries lie within 30 minutes' drive of Wangaratta, some with food and accommodation.
In the King Valley, Italian migrants of the 1940s and 1950s switched from tobacco to European wine varieties, and the valley is known for sangiovese, nebbiolo and barbera.
Warby-Ovens National Park, about 10 minutes from the city, is good for bushwalking but can get very hot in summer.

experiences: Taste wines in Glenrowan and the King Valley
Follow the Ned Kelly story at Glenrowan

tips.title: Warby Ranges get hot
tips.detail: Bushwalking in Warby-Ovens National Park can be very hot in summer, so walk in the cooler months or early in the day.

tips.title: Ride the rail trail
tips.detail: The Murray to the Mountains Rail Trail is sealed for almost its whole 95 km, so ordinary bikes cope.

best_months.rationale: Autumn and spring avoid the summer heat noted for the Warby Ranges.
